1.3 Equivalences of categories

We now develop some basic properties of the equivalences introduced in Definition 1.1.5.

Proposition 1.3.1. Let \(f\colon C\to D\) be a functor. For \(f\) to be an equivalence, it suffices that the following properties hold for every category \(T\):

naive-bijection-isEquiv

Derivation, checked

naive-bijection-isEquiv : {C D : CAT} {f : MAP C D}
  → NaiveBijection f → IsEquiv f
Proof / implementation
naive-bijection-isEquiv {C} {D} {f} b =
  --! begin naive-bijection-inverse-data
  let chosen = NaiveBijection.lift b (id D)
      g = FunctorLift.lift chosen
      ε = FunctorLift.comparison chosen
  --! end naive-bijection-inverse-data
      --! begin naive-bijection-reflection
      η = NaiveBijection.reflect b (g ∘ f) (id C)
        ((comp-unitʳ f) ⁻¹ ∙ (comp-unitˡ f ∙ ((ε ▷ f) ∙ (comp-assoc f g f) ⁻¹)))
      --! end naive-bijection-reflection
  in record { inverse = g ; sectionIso = η ⁻¹ ; retractionIso = ε ⁻¹ }

Proof

Proof. Apply the second property to \(\id _D\) to obtain \(g\colon D\to C\) and \(fg=\id _D\). The associator, this identification, and the unitors identify \(f(gf)\) with \(f\id _C\). The first property, with \(T=C\), gives \(gf=\id _C\). □

Definition 1.3.2 (Section/retraction). Consider a functor \(f\colon C \to D\). A section of \(f\) is a functor \(s\colon D \to C\) equipped with an identification \(fs = \id _D\). A retraction of \(f\) is a functor \(r\colon D \to C\) equipped with an identification \(\id _C = rf\).

Lemma 1.3.3. A functor \(f\colon C \to D\) is an equivalence if and only if it admits both a section \(s\) and a retraction \(r\). In this case there exists an identification \(s = r\) and \(s\) is an inverse of \(f\).

Agda Inverse on both sides implies equivalence

section-retraction-isEquiv

Derivation, checked

section-retraction-isEquiv : {C D : CAT} {f : MAP C D}
  → Section f → Retraction f → IsEquiv f
Proof / implementation
section-retraction-isEquiv {f = f} s r = record
  { inverse = Section.section s
  ; sectionIso = ((section-retraction-iso s r) ⁻¹ ▷ f) ∙ Retraction.comparison r
  ; retractionIso = (Section.comparison s) ⁻¹ }

section-retraction-iso

Derivation, checked

section-retraction-iso : {C D : CAT} {f : MAP C D}
  (s : Section f) (r : Retraction f)
  → (Section.section s) =₁ (Retraction.retraction r)
Proof / implementation
section-retraction-iso {f = f} s r =
  let u = Section.section s
      v = Retraction.retraction r
  in comp-unitʳ v ∙ ((v ◁ Section.comparison s) ∙
     (comp-assoc u f v ∙ ((Retraction.comparison r ▷ u) ∙ (comp-unitˡ u) ⁻¹)))

Proof

Proof. If \(f\) is an equivalence with inverse \(g\colon D \to C\), then clearly \(g\) is both a section and a retraction of \(f\). Conversely, given a section \(s\colon D \to C\), \(fs = \id _D\) and a retraction \(r\colon D \to C\), \(\id _C = rf\), we obtain an identification \(s = r\) by composing the following chain of identifications: Agda\[ s = \id _C \circ s = (r \circ f) \circ s = r \circ (f \circ s) = r \circ \id _D = r. \] It follows that \(f\) is an equivalence with inverse \(s\), since there are identifications \(fs = \id _{D}\) and \(sf = rf = \id _{C}\). □

Agda Inverse on both sides implies equivalence step 1

section-retraction-iso : {C D : CAT} {f : MAP C D}
  (s : Section f) (r : Retraction f)

Proof / implementation

Lemma 1.3.5. If \(f\colon C \to D\) and \(f'\colon D \to E\) are equivalences with inverses \(g\colon D \to C\) and \(g'\colon E \to D\), then also the composite \(f'f\colon C \to E\) is an equivalence with inverse \(gg'\colon E \to C\).

Agda Composite of equivalences

equiv-compose

Derivation, checked

equiv-compose : {C D E : CAT} (f : MAP C D) (g : MAP D E)
  → IsEquiv f → IsEquiv g → IsEquiv (g ∘ f)
Proof / implementation
equiv-compose {C} {D} {E} f g ef eg =
  let u : MAP D C
      u = IsEquiv.inverse ef
      v : MAP E D
      v = IsEquiv.inverse eg
      --! begin equiv-compose-left
      left : ((u ∘ v) ∘ (g ∘ f)) =₁ (id C)
      left = (IsEquiv.sectionIso ef) ⁻¹ ∙
        ((u ◁ comp-unitˡ f) ∙ ((u ◁ ((IsEquiv.sectionIso eg) ⁻¹ ▷ f)) ∙
        ((u ◁ (comp-assoc f g v) ⁻¹) ∙ comp-assoc (g ∘ f) v u)))
      --! end equiv-compose-left
      --! begin equiv-compose-right
      right : ((g ∘ f) ∘ (u ∘ v)) =₁ (id E)
      right = (IsEquiv.retractionIso eg) ⁻¹ ∙
        ((g ◁ comp-unitˡ v) ∙ ((g ◁ ((IsEquiv.retractionIso ef) ⁻¹ ▷ v)) ∙
        ((g ◁ (comp-assoc v u f) ⁻¹) ∙ comp-assoc (u ∘ v) f g)))
      --! end equiv-compose-right
  in record { inverse = u ∘ v ; sectionIso = left ⁻¹ ; retractionIso = right ⁻¹ }

Proof

Proof. If \(g\) and \(f\) are equivalences, then so is \(gf\) by Lemma 1.3.5. If \(f\) and \(gf\) are equivalences, then we may rewrite \(g\) as the composite \(g = g \circ \id _{D} = g \circ f \circ f^{-1} = gf \circ f^{-1}\), so that \(g\) is the composite of two equivalences and hence itself an equivalence. A similar argument shows that \(f\) is an equivalence whenever \(g\) and \(gf\) are equivalences. □

Derivation, checked

two-out-of-six : {C D E F : CAT}

Proof / implementation
two-out-of-six f g h egf ehg =
  --! begin two-out-of-six-inverses
  let u = IsEquiv.inverse egf
      v = IsEquiv.inverse ehg
  --! end two-out-of-six-inverses

      eg = section-retraction-isEquiv s r
      --! end two-out-of-six-middle
      --! begin two-out-of-six-conclusion
      ef = equiv-cancel-left f g eg egf
      eh = equiv-cancel-right g h eg ehg
  in record { first = ef ; middle = eg ; last = eh
            ; composite = equiv-compose (g ∘ f) h egf eh }
      --! end two-out-of-six-conclusion

Proof

Proof. Consider the functors \(f' := f \circ (gf)^{-1}\colon E \to D\) and \(h' := (hg)^{-1} \circ h \colon E \to D\). Then there are identifications Agda\[ g \circ f' = g \circ f \circ (gf)^{-1} = gf \circ (gf)^{-1} = \id _{E} \] and Agda\[ h' \circ g = (hg)^{-1} \circ h \circ g = (hg)^{-1} \circ hg = \id _{D}. \] Hence it follows from Lemma 1.3.3 that \(g\) is an equivalence. In light of Lemma 1.3.6, we then get that also \(f\) and \(h\) are equivalences, and then so is \(hgf\). □

Definition 1.3.8. We say that a functor \(f\colon C \to D\) is a retract of a functor \(f'\colon C' \to D'\) if there exists a commutative diagram of the form

Agda Retract

RetractDiagram

Definition, checked

record RetractDiagram {C D C′ D′ : CAT} (f : MAP C D) (f′ : MAP C′ D′) : Set m where
  field
    g : MAP C C′
    h : MAP C′ C
    k : MAP D D′
    j : MAP D′ D
    leftSquare : (f′ ∘ g) =₁ (k ∘ f)
    rightSquare : (f ∘ h) =₁ (j ∘ f′)
    α : (id C) =₁ (h ∘ g)
    β : (j ∘ k) =₁ (id D)

  loop : f =₁ f
  loop = comp-unitˡ f ∙ ((β ▷ f) ∙
    ((comp-assoc f k j) ⁻¹ ∙ ((j ◁ leftSquare) ∙
    (comp-assoc g f′ j ∙ ((rightSquare ▷ g) ∙
    ((comp-assoc g h f) ⁻¹ ∙ ((f ◁ α) ∙ (comp-unitʳ f) ⁻¹)))))))

Lemma 1.3.9. Assume that \(f\colon C \to D\) is a retract of \(f'\colon C' \to D'\). If \(f'\) is an equivalence, then so is \(f\).

Agda Equivalences closed under retracts

retract-isEquiv

Derivation, checked

retract-isEquiv : {C D C′ D′ : CAT} {f : MAP C D} {f′ : MAP C′ D′}
  → Retract f f′ → IsEquiv f′ → IsEquiv f
Proof / implementation
retract-isEquiv {f = f} {f′} R e =
  let open RetractDiagram (Retract.diagram R)
      u = IsEquiv.inverse e
      --! begin retract-inverse
      w = h ∘ (u ∘ k)
      --! end retract-inverse
      --! begin retract-counit
      counit = β ∙ ((j ◁ comp-unitˡ k) ∙
        ((j ◁ ((IsEquiv.retractionIso e) ⁻¹ ▷ k)) ∙
        ((j ◁ (comp-assoc k u f′) ⁻¹) ∙
        (comp-assoc (u ∘ k) f′ j ∙ ((rightSquare ▷ (u ∘ k)) ∙
        (comp-assoc (u ∘ k) h f) ⁻¹)))))
      --! end retract-counit
      --! begin retract-inverse-unit
      inverseUnit = α ⁻¹ ∙ ((h ◁ comp-unitˡ g) ∙
        ((h ◁ ((IsEquiv.sectionIso e) ⁻¹ ▷ g)) ∙
        ((h ◁ (comp-assoc g f′ u) ⁻¹) ∙
        ((h ◁ (u ◁ leftSquare ⁻¹)) ∙
        ((h ◁ comp-assoc f k u) ∙ comp-assoc f (u ∘ k) h)))))
      --! end retract-inverse-unit
  in record { inverse = w ; sectionIso = inverseUnit ⁻¹ ; retractionIso = counit ⁻¹ }

Proof

Proof. Let \((f')^{-1}\colon D' \to C'\) be an inverse of \(f'\). We claim that the composite \(w := h \circ (f')^{-1} \circ k\colon D \to C\) is inverse to \(f\). Indeed, we have identifications Agda\[ f \circ w = f \circ h \circ (f')^{-1} \circ k = j \circ f' \circ (f')^{-1} \circ k = j \circ k = \id _{D} \] and Agda\[ w \circ f = h \circ (f')^{-1} \circ k \circ f = h \circ (f')^{-1} \circ f' \circ g = h \circ g = \id _{C}. \] This finishes the proof. □

Lemma 1.3.10. Prewhiskering or postwhiskering by an equivalence induces equivalences of animae of identifications.

Agda Whiskering by equivalence

postWhisker-isEquiv

Derivation, checked

postWhisker-isEquiv : {B C D : CAT} (F : MAP C D) → IsEquiv F
  → (f g : MAP B C) → IsEquiv (postWhisker {f = f} {g} F)
Proof / implementation
postWhisker-isEquiv F e f g =
  let G = IsEquiv.inverse e
      first = post-composite f g F G
        (post-change ((IsEquiv.sectionIso e) ⁻¹) f g (post-id f g))
      second = post-composite (F ∘ f) (F ∘ g) G F
        (post-change ((IsEquiv.retractionIso e) ⁻¹) (F ∘ f) (F ∘ g)
          (post-id (F ∘ f) (F ∘ g)))
  in TwoOutOfSix.first (two-out-of-six (postWhisker F) (postWhisker G)
       (postWhisker F) first second)

Proof

Let \(F\colon C\to D\) have inverse \(G\), and consider two functors \(a,b\colon T\to C\). We wish to show that the first functor \(F \star -\) in the following diagram is an equivalence: \[ (a= b)\xrightarrow {F\star -}(Fa= Fb) \xrightarrow {G\star -}(GFa= GFb) \xrightarrow {F\star -}(FGFa= FGFb). \] Interchange with \(GF=\id _C\) identifies the composite of the first two functors with transport along the identifications \(GFa = a\) and \(b = GFb\), and so that composite is an equivalence. The composite of the last two is an equivalence for the same reason, using \(FG=\id _D\), and so the claim follows from the 2-out-of-6 property. Prewhiskering is treated in the same way. □

post-change

Derivation, checked

post-change : {B C D : CAT} {F G : MAP C D}
  (τ : F =₁ G) (f g : MAP B C)
  → IsEquiv (postWhisker {f = f} {g} G) → IsEquiv (postWhisker {f = f} {g} F)
Proof / implementation
post-change {F = F} {G} τ f g = square-left (postWhisker F) (postWhisker G)
  (τ ▷ f) (τ ▷ g)
  (isoComp-cong (comp-unitʳ (postWhisker G)) (idIso _) ∙
   (interchange-fixedOuter F G f g τ ∙
    (isoComp-cong (idIso _) (comp-unitʳ (postWhisker F))) ⁻¹))

square-left

Derivation, checked

square-left : {X C D : CAT} {f g f′ g′ : MAP C D}
  (u : MAP X (f ＝ g)) (v : MAP X (f′ ＝ g′))
  (α : f =₁ f′) (β : g =₁ g′)
  → (const β ∙ u) =₁ (v ∙ const α) → IsEquiv v → IsEquiv u
Proof / implementation
square-left u v α β κ ev = equiv-cancel-left u (leftMultiply β)
  (leftMultiply-isEquiv β)
  (equiv-transport ((left-evaluate β u) ⁻¹ ∙ (κ ⁻¹ ∙ right-evaluate α v))
    (equiv-compose v (rightMultiply α) ev (rightMultiply-isEquiv α)))

Agda Whiskering by equivalence step 3

postWhisker-isEquiv

Derivation, checked

postWhisker-isEquiv : {B C D : CAT} (F : MAP C D) → IsEquiv F
  → (f g : MAP B C) → IsEquiv (postWhisker {f = f} {g} F)
Proof / implementation
postWhisker-isEquiv F e f g =
  let G = IsEquiv.inverse e
      first = post-composite f g F G
        (post-change ((IsEquiv.sectionIso e) ⁻¹) f g (post-id f g))
      second = post-composite (F ∘ f) (F ∘ g) G F
        (post-change ((IsEquiv.retractionIso e) ⁻¹) (F ∘ f) (F ∘ g)
          (post-id (F ∘ f) (F ∘ g)))
  in TwoOutOfSix.first (two-out-of-six (postWhisker F) (postWhisker G)
       (postWhisker F) first second)

two-out-of-six

Derivation, checked

two-out-of-six : {C D E F : CAT}
  (f : MAP C D) (g : MAP D E) (h : MAP E F)
  → IsEquiv (g ∘ f) → IsEquiv (h ∘ g) → TwoOutOfSix f g h
Proof / implementation
two-out-of-six f g h egf ehg =
  --! begin two-out-of-six-inverses
  let u = IsEquiv.inverse egf
      v = IsEquiv.inverse ehg
  --! end two-out-of-six-inverses
      --! begin two-out-of-six-section
      s = record { section = f ∘ u
                 ; comparison = (IsEquiv.retractionIso egf) ⁻¹ ∙ (comp-assoc u f g) ⁻¹ }
      --! end two-out-of-six-section
      --! begin two-out-of-six-retraction
      r = record { retraction = v ∘ h
                 ; comparison = (comp-assoc g h v) ⁻¹ ∙ IsEquiv.sectionIso ehg }
      --! end two-out-of-six-retraction
      --! begin two-out-of-six-middle
      eg = section-retraction-isEquiv s r
      --! end two-out-of-six-middle
      --! begin two-out-of-six-conclusion
      ef = equiv-cancel-left f g eg egf
      eh = equiv-cancel-right g h eg ehg
  in record { first = ef ; middle = eg ; last = eh
            ; composite = equiv-compose (g ∘ f) h egf eh }
      --! end two-out-of-six-conclusion

pre-change

Derivation, checked

pre-change : {B C D : CAT} {h k : MAP B C}
  (σ : h =₁ k) (f g : MAP C D)
  → IsEquiv (preWhisker {f = f} {g} k) → IsEquiv (preWhisker {f = f} {g} h)
Proof / implementation
pre-change {h = h} {k} σ f g = square-left (preWhisker h) (preWhisker k)
  (f ◁ σ) (g ◁ σ)
  (isoComp-cong (comp-unitʳ (preWhisker k)) (idIso _) ∙
   ((interchange-fixedInner f g h k σ) ⁻¹ ∙
    (isoComp-cong (idIso _) (comp-unitʳ (preWhisker h))) ⁻¹))

pre-composite

Derivation, checked

pre-composite : {A B C D : CAT} (f g : MAP C D) (k : MAP B C) (l : MAP A B)

  → IsEquiv (preWhisker l ∘ preWhisker {f = f} {g} k)

Consequently an equivalence lifts a specified identification, together with an identification of its image with that identification. Applying the same result to functors into an anima of identifications also lifts identifications between identifications.

equiv-reflect {f = f} e u v α =

Proof

Proof. We need to provide identifications \((\pr _2,\pr _1) \circ (\pr _2,\pr _1) = \id _{C \times D}\) and \((\pr _2,\pr _1) \circ (\pr _2,\pr _1) = \id _{D \times C}\). By symmetry, it will suffice to produce the first identification. For this, it will in turn suffice to produce identifications after composing with the functors \(\pr _1\) and \(\pr _2\). For the composition with \(\pr _1\) we compute that \[ \pr _1 \circ ((\pr _2,\pr _1) \circ (\pr _2,\pr _1)) = (\pr _1 \circ (\pr _2,\pr _1)) \circ (\pr _2,\pr _1) = \pr _2 \circ (\pr _2,\pr _1) = \pr _1, \] which is indeed identified with \(\pr _1 \circ \id _{C \times D}\). The case for composition with \(\pr _2\) is analogous. This finishes the proof. □

Proof

Proof. The composite \(\pr _1 \circ (\id _{C}, p_{C})\colon C \to C\) is identified with \(\id _{C}\) by the defining property of \((\id _{C}, p_{C})\). To show that the composite \((\id _{C}, p_{C}) \circ \pr _1\colon C \times * \to C \times *\) is identified with \(\id _{C \times *}\), it will suffice to do so after composing with \(\pr _1\) and with \(\pr _2\). The case for \(\pr _2\) is clear, since any two functors \(C \times * \to *\) are identified. In the case of \(\pr _1\) we compute \[ \pr _1 \circ ((\id _{C}, p_{C}) \circ \pr _1) = (\pr _1 \circ (\id _{C}, p_{C})) \circ \pr _1 = \id _{C} \circ \pr _1 = \pr _1 = \pr _1 \circ \id _{C \times *}, \] where the first identification is associativity, the second is the relation proved in the first paragraph, and the third and fourth are unitality. This finishes the proof. □

Construction 1.3.15 (Pairing of identifications). Given functors \(f,f'\colon T \to C\) and \(g,g'\colon T \to D\), pairing defines a functor \[ (-,-)\colon (f=f')\times (g=g')\longrightarrow ((f,g)=(f',g')). \] For \(\varphi :f=f'\) and \(\psi :g=g'\), its value \((\varphi ,\psi )\) is equipped with identifications \begin {align*} \beta ^1_{f',g'}\circ \bigl (\pr _1\star (\varphi ,\psi )\bigr ) &=\varphi \circ \beta ^1_{f,g},\\ \beta ^2_{f',g'}\circ \bigl (\pr _2\star (\varphi ,\psi )\bigr ) &=\psi \circ \beta ^2_{f,g}. \end {align*}

There are identifications \[ (\id _f,\id _g)=\id _{(f,g)},\qquad (\varphi '\circ \varphi ,\psi '\circ \psi ) =(\varphi ',\psi ')\circ (\varphi ,\psi ), \] where \(\varphi ':f'=f''\) and \(\psi ':g'=g''\).

Proof

Proof. Under the identifications \(\beta ^1_{f,g}:\pr _1(f,g)=f\) and \(\beta ^2_{f,g}:\pr _2(f,g)=g\), \(\phi \) and \(\psi \) correspond to two absolute objects of the two factors of the following product: \[ \bigl (\pr _1(f,g)=\pr _1(f',g')\bigr ) \times \bigl (\pr _2(f,g)=\pr _2(f',g')\bigr ). \] Since this product is equivalent to the anima \((f,g) = (f',g')\) by Axiom B.2, this provides the identification \((\phi ,\psi )\) with the two claimed identification.

We leave the identity law and composition law as exercises for the reader. □

pairing-absolute

Derivation, checked

pairing-absolute : {X C D : CAT} {f f′ : MAP X C} {g g′ : MAP X D}
  (α : f =₁ f′) (β : g =₁ g′) → (pairing α β) =₂ (pair-cong α β)
Proof / implementation
pairing-absolute {f = f} {f′} {g} {g′} α β =
  let first = isoComp-cong (const-One ((pair-β₁ f′ g′) ⁻¹))
        (isoComp-cong (idIso α) (const-One (pair-β₁ f g)))
      second = isoComp-cong (const-One ((pair-β₂ f′ g′) ⁻¹))
        (isoComp-cong (idIso β) (const-One (pair-β₂ f g)))
      back = IsEquiv.inverse (product-isoMap-isEquiv (pair f g) (pair f′ g′))
  in back ◁ pair-cong first second

Lemma 1.3.16 (Pairing and precomposition). Let \(f\colon T\to C\), \(g\colon T\to D\), and \(\sigma \colon S\to T\) be functors. Pairing commutes with precomposition: there is an identification \[ (f,g)\circ \sigma =(f\circ \sigma ,g\circ \sigma ). \] This comparison is compatible with identifications of the input functors, with successive precomposition, and with precomposition by an identity functor, using the associativity and unitality identifications.

family-pair-pre-full

Derivation, checked

family-pair-pre-full : {A R X C D : CAT}
  {f f′ : MAP X C} {g g′ : MAP X D} {r s : MAP R X}
  (α : MAP A (f ＝ f′)) (β : MAP A (g ＝ g′)) (γ : MAP A (r ＝ s))
  → (pairing (α ⋆ γ) (β ⋆ γ) ∙ const (pair-pre f g r)) =₁
      (const (pair-pre f′ g′ s) ∙ (pairing α β ⋆ γ))
Proof / implementation
family-pair-pre-full {f = f} {f′} {g} {g′} {r} {s} α β γ =
  let outer = pairing (α ▷ s) (β ▷ s)
      inner = pairing (f ◁ γ) (g ◁ γ)
      before = const (pair-pre f g r)
      middle = const (pair-pre f g s)
      after = const (pair-pre f′ g′ s)
      input = pairing α β ▷ s
      substitution = pair f g ◁ γ
  in assoc after input substitution ∙
    (isoComp-cong (family-pair-pre-inputs α β s) (idIso substitution) ∙
      ((assoc outer middle substitution) ⁻¹ ∙
        (isoComp-cong (idIso outer) (family-pair-pre-substitution f g γ) ∙
          (assoc outer inner before ∙
            isoComp-cong (pairing-composition (α ▷ s) (f ◁ γ) (β ▷ s) (g ◁ γ))
              (idIso before)))))

pair-pre-id

Derivation, checked

pair-pre-id : {X C D : CAT} (f : MAP X C) (g : MAP X D)
  →
      (pair-cong (comp-unitʳ f) (comp-unitʳ g) ∙ pair-pre f g (id X)) =₂
      (comp-unitʳ (pair f g))
Proof / implementation
pair-pre-id {X} f g =
  let h = pair f g
      h′ = pair (f ∘ id X) (g ∘ id X)
      ρ = pair-cong (comp-unitʳ f) (comp-unitʳ g)
      τ = pair-pre f g (id X)
  in pair-iso-extensionality
    (unit-projection pr₁ h h′ f (pair-β₁ f g) (pair-β₁ (f ∘ id X) (g ∘ id X)) ρ τ
      (pair-cong-triangle₁ (comp-unitʳ f) (comp-unitʳ g)) (pair-pre-triangle₁ f g (id X)))
    (unit-projection pr₂ h h′ g (pair-β₂ f g) (pair-β₂ (f ∘ id X) (g ∘ id X)) ρ τ
      (pair-cong-triangle₂ (comp-unitʳ f) (comp-unitʳ g)) (pair-pre-triangle₂ f g (id X)))

pairing-absolute

Derivation, checked

pairing-absolute : {X C D : CAT} {f f′ : MAP X C} {g g′ : MAP X D}
  (α : f =₁ f′) (β : g =₁ g′) → (pairing α β) =₂ (pair-cong α β)
Proof / implementation
pairing-absolute {f = f} {f′} {g} {g′} α β =
  let first = isoComp-cong (const-One ((pair-β₁ f′ g′) ⁻¹))
        (isoComp-cong (idIso α) (const-One (pair-β₁ f g)))
      second = isoComp-cong (const-One ((pair-β₂ f′ g′) ⁻¹))
        (isoComp-cong (idIso β) (const-One (pair-β₂ f g)))
      back = IsEquiv.inverse (product-isoMap-isEquiv (pair f g) (pair f′ g′))
  in back ◁ pair-cong first second

Derivation, checked

productMap-comp-family : {A C C′ C″ D D′ D″ : CAT}
  {f f′ : MAP C C′} {g g′ : MAP D D′}
  {F F′ : MAP C′ C″} {G G′ : MAP D′ D″}
  (α : MAP A (f ＝ f′)) (β : MAP A (g ＝ g′))
  (θ : MAP A (F ＝ F′)) (ψ : MAP A (G ＝ G′))
  →
      (const (productMap-comp f′ F′ g′ G′) ∙ (productFamily θ ψ ⋆ productFamily α β)) =₁
      (productFamily (θ ⋆ α) (ψ ⋆ β) ∙ const (productMap-comp f F g G))
Proof / implementation
productMap-comp-family {f = f} {f′} {g} {g′} {F} {F′} {G} {G′} α β θ ψ =
  let c = const (productMap-comp f F g G)
      c₁ = const (productMap-comp f′ F g′ G)
      c₂ = const (productMap-comp f′ F′ g′ G′)
      u = productMap F G ◁ productFamily α β
      v = productFamily θ ψ ▷ productMap f′ g′
      a = productFamily (F ◁ α) (G ◁ β)
      b = productFamily (θ ▷ f′) (ψ ▷ g′)
  in isoComp-cong ((productFamily-composition (θ ▷ f′) (F ◁ α) (ψ ▷ g′) (G ◁ β)) ⁻¹) (idIso c) ∙
    ((assoc b a c) ⁻¹ ∙
    (isoComp-cong (idIso b) (productMap-comp-family-inner α β F G) ∙
    (assoc b c₁ u ∙
    (isoComp-cong (productMap-comp-family-outer f′ g′ θ ψ) (idIso u) ∙
     (assoc c₂ v u) ⁻¹))))

productMap-unitˡ

Derivation, checked

productMap-unitˡ : {C C′ D D′ : CAT} (f : MAP C C′) (g : MAP D D′)
  →
      (productMap-cong (comp-unitˡ f) (comp-unitˡ g) ∙
        productMap-comp f (id C′) g (id D′)) =₂
      (comp-unitˡ (productMap f g) ∙ (productMap-id C′ D′ ▷ productMap f g))
Proof / implementation
productMap-unitˡ {C} {C′} {D} {D′} f g =
  let h = productMap f g
      h′ = productMap (id C′ ∘ f) (id D′ ∘ g)
      J = productMap (id C′) (id D′)
      δ = productMap-id C′ D′
      b = pair-β₁ (f ∘ pr₁) (g ∘ pr₂)
      d = pair-β₂ (f ∘ pr₁) (g ∘ pr₂)
      b′ = pair-β₁ ((id C′ ∘ f) ∘ pr₁) ((id D′ ∘ g) ∘ pr₂)
      d′ = pair-β₂ ((id C′ ∘ f) ∘ pr₁) ((id D′ ∘ g) ∘ pr₂)
      bJ = pair-β₁ (id C′ ∘ pr₁) (id D′ ∘ pr₂)
      dJ = pair-β₂ (id C′ ∘ pr₁) (id D′ ∘ pr₂)
      out = productMap-cong (comp-unitˡ f) (comp-unitˡ g)
      step = productMap-comp f (id C′) g (id D′)
      e = coordinate-comparison pr₁ f pr₁ h b (id C′)
      k = coordinate-comparison pr₂ g pr₂ h d (id D′)
  in pair-iso-extensionality
    (left-unit-projection pr₁ f pr₁ h h′ J δ b b′ bJ out step
      (productMap-id-triangle₁ C′ D′)
      (pair-cong-triangle₁ (comp-unitˡ f ▷ pr₁) (comp-unitˡ g ▷ pr₂))
      (pair-pre-cong-triangle₁ (id C′ ∘ pr₁) (id D′ ∘ pr₂) h e k))
    (left-unit-projection pr₂ g pr₂ h h′ J δ d d′ dJ out step
      (productMap-id-triangle₂ C′ D′)
      (pair-cong-triangle₂ (comp-unitˡ f ▷ pr₁) (comp-unitˡ g ▷ pr₂))
      (pair-pre-cong-triangle₂ (id C′ ∘ pr₁) (id D′ ∘ pr₂) h e k))

productIsoMap-at

Derivation, checked

productIsoMap-at : {C C′ D D′ : CAT}
  {f f′ : MAP C C′} {g g′ : MAP D D′}
  (α : f =₁ f′) (β : g =₁ g′)
  → (productIsoMap f f′ g g′ ∘ pair α β) =₂ (productMap-cong α β)
Proof / implementation
productIsoMap-at {f = f} {f′} {g} {g′} α β =
  let input = pair (preWhisker pr₁ ∘ pr₁) (preWhisker pr₂ ∘ pr₂)
      output = pairIsoMap (f ∘ pr₁) (f′ ∘ pr₁) (g ∘ pr₂) (g′ ∘ pr₂)
      point = pair α β
      first = (preWhisker pr₁ ◁ pair-β₁ α β) ∙ comp-assoc point pr₁ (preWhisker pr₁)
      second = (preWhisker pr₂ ◁ pair-β₂ α β) ∙ comp-assoc point pr₂ (preWhisker pr₂)
  in pairIsoMap-at (α ▷ pr₁) (β ▷ pr₂) ∙
    ((output ◁ (pair-cong first second ∙
      pair-pre (preWhisker pr₁ ∘ pr₁) (preWhisker pr₂ ∘ pr₂) point)) ∙
      comp-assoc point input output)

family-pair-pre-full

Derivation, checked

family-pair-pre-full : {A R X C D : CAT}
  {f f′ : MAP X C} {g g′ : MAP X D} {r s : MAP R X}
  (α : MAP A (f ＝ f′)) (β : MAP A (g ＝ g′)) (γ : MAP A (r ＝ s))
  → (pairing (α ⋆ γ) (β ⋆ γ) ∙ const (pair-pre f g r)) =₁
      (const (pair-pre f′ g′ s) ∙ (pairing α β ⋆ γ))
Proof / implementation
family-pair-pre-full {f = f} {f′} {g} {g′} {r} {s} α β γ =
  let outer = pairing (α ▷ s) (β ▷ s)
      inner = pairing (f ◁ γ) (g ◁ γ)
      before = const (pair-pre f g r)
      middle = const (pair-pre f g s)
      after = const (pair-pre f′ g′ s)
      input = pairing α β ▷ s
      substitution = pair f g ◁ γ
  in assoc after input substitution ∙
    (isoComp-cong (family-pair-pre-inputs α β s) (idIso substitution) ∙
      ((assoc outer middle substitution) ⁻¹ ∙
        (isoComp-cong (idIso outer) (family-pair-pre-substitution f g γ) ∙
          (assoc outer inner before ∙
            isoComp-cong (pairing-composition (α ▷ s) (f ◁ γ) (β ▷ s) (g ◁ γ))
              (idIso before)))))

Proof

Proof. After composition with \(\pr _1\) and \(\pr _2\), both sides identify with \(f\circ \sigma \) and \(g\circ \sigma \), respectively. The product axiom therefore supplies the comparison, with these prescribed projections. Its compatibilities can likewise be checked after applying both projections, where they reduce to the coherence laws for composition and identifications. For compatibility with identity functors, one also uses \[ \rho _{ab}=(a\star \rho _b)\circ \alpha _{\id ,b,a} \tag{1.1}\] for composable functors \(b,a\). This follows by prewhiskering with the identity, applying the pentagon for \(a,b,\id ,\id \) and the triangle identities, and cancelling by Lemma 1.3.10. We leave the remaining checks to the reader. □

pair-pre-id : {X C D : CAT} (f : MAP X C) (g : MAP X D)
  →
      (pair-cong (comp-unitʳ f) (comp-unitʳ g) ∙ pair-pre f g (id X)) =₂

Proof / implementation
pair-pre-id {X} f g =
  let h = pair f g
      h′ = pair (f ∘ id X) (g ∘ id X)

    (unit-projection pr₁ h h′ f (pair-β₁ f g) (pair-β₁ (f ∘ id X) (g ∘ id X)) ρ τ

Construction 1.3.17. The formation of products of categories is functorial: given \(f\colon C\to C'\) and \(g\colon D\to D'\), we obtain a functor \[ f\times g:=(f\pr _1,g\pr _2):C\times D\to C'\times D'. \] For identifications \(\varphi : f = f'\) and \(\psi : g = g'\) between functors with these same sources and targets, we define \[ \varphi \times \psi :=(\varphi \star \pr _1,\psi \star \pr _2). \] This gives a functor on the product of the two animae of identifications. It preserves identity identifications and vertical composition by Construction 1.3.15 and the corresponding laws for whiskering.

productIsoMap-at

Derivation, checked

productIsoMap-at : {C C′ D D′ : CAT}
  {f f′ : MAP C C′} {g g′ : MAP D D′}
  (α : f =₁ f′) (β : g =₁ g′)
  → (productIsoMap f f′ g g′ ∘ pair α β) =₂ (productMap-cong α β)
Proof / implementation
productIsoMap-at {f = f} {f′} {g} {g′} α β =
  let input = pair (preWhisker pr₁ ∘ pr₁) (preWhisker pr₂ ∘ pr₂)
      output = pairIsoMap (f ∘ pr₁) (f′ ∘ pr₁) (g ∘ pr₂) (g′ ∘ pr₂)
      point = pair α β
      first = (preWhisker pr₁ ◁ pair-β₁ α β) ∙ comp-assoc point pr₁ (preWhisker pr₁)
      second = (preWhisker pr₂ ◁ pair-β₂ α β) ∙ comp-assoc point pr₂ (preWhisker pr₂)
  in pairIsoMap-at (α ▷ pr₁) (β ▷ pr₂) ∙
    ((output ◁ (pair-cong first second ∙
      pair-pre (preWhisker pr₁ ∘ pr₁) (preWhisker pr₂ ∘ pr₂) point)) ∙
      comp-assoc point input output)

productMap-comp-family : {A C C′ C″ D D′ D″ : CAT}

  {F F′ : MAP C′ C″} {G G′ : MAP D′ D″}
  (α : MAP A (f ＝ f′)) (β : MAP A (g ＝ g′))
  (θ : MAP A (F ＝ F′)) (ψ : MAP A (G ＝ G′))
  →
      (const (productMap-comp f′ F′ g′ G′) ∙ (productFamily θ ψ ⋆ productFamily α β)) =₁
      (productFamily (θ ⋆ α) (ψ ⋆ β) ∙ const (productMap-comp f F g G))
Proof / implementation
productMap-comp-family {f = f} {f′} {g} {g′} {F} {F′} {G} {G′} α β θ ψ =
  let c = const (productMap-comp f F g G)
      c₁ = const (productMap-comp f′ F g′ G)
      c₂ = const (productMap-comp f′ F′ g′ G′)
      u = productMap F G ◁ productFamily α β
      v = productFamily θ ψ ▷ productMap f′ g′
      a = productFamily (F ◁ α) (G ◁ β)
      b = productFamily (θ ▷ f′) (ψ ▷ g′)
  in isoComp-cong ((productFamily-composition (θ ▷ f′) (F ◁ α) (ψ ▷ g′) (G ◁ β)) ⁻¹) (idIso c) ∙
    ((assoc b a c) ⁻¹ ∙
    (isoComp-cong (idIso b) (productMap-comp-family-inner α β F G) ∙
    (assoc b c₁ u ∙
    (isoComp-cong (productMap-comp-family-outer f′ g′ θ ψ) (idIso u) ∙
     (assoc c₂ v u) ⁻¹))))

productMap-unitˡ

Derivation, checked

productMap-unitˡ : {C C′ D D′ : CAT} (f : MAP C C′) (g : MAP D D′)
  →
      (productMap-cong (comp-unitˡ f) (comp-unitˡ g) ∙
        productMap-comp f (id C′) g (id D′)) =₂
      (comp-unitˡ (productMap f g) ∙ (productMap-id C′ D′ ▷ productMap f g))
Proof / implementation
productMap-unitˡ {C} {C′} {D} {D′} f g =
  let h = productMap f g
      h′ = productMap (id C′ ∘ f) (id D′ ∘ g)
      J = productMap (id C′) (id D′)
      δ = productMap-id C′ D′
      b = pair-β₁ (f ∘ pr₁) (g ∘ pr₂)
      d = pair-β₂ (f ∘ pr₁) (g ∘ pr₂)
      b′ = pair-β₁ ((id C′ ∘ f) ∘ pr₁) ((id D′ ∘ g) ∘ pr₂)
      d′ = pair-β₂ ((id C′ ∘ f) ∘ pr₁) ((id D′ ∘ g) ∘ pr₂)
      bJ = pair-β₁ (id C′ ∘ pr₁) (id D′ ∘ pr₂)
      dJ = pair-β₂ (id C′ ∘ pr₁) (id D′ ∘ pr₂)
      out = productMap-cong (comp-unitˡ f) (comp-unitˡ g)
      step = productMap-comp f (id C′) g (id D′)
      e = coordinate-comparison pr₁ f pr₁ h b (id C′)
      k = coordinate-comparison pr₂ g pr₂ h d (id D′)
  in pair-iso-extensionality
    (left-unit-projection pr₁ f pr₁ h h′ J δ b b′ bJ out step
      (productMap-id-triangle₁ C′ D′)
      (pair-cong-triangle₁ (comp-unitˡ f ▷ pr₁) (comp-unitˡ g ▷ pr₂))
      (pair-pre-cong-triangle₁ (id C′ ∘ pr₁) (id D′ ∘ pr₂) h e k))
    (left-unit-projection pr₂ g pr₂ h h′ J δ d d′ dJ out step
      (productMap-id-triangle₂ C′ D′)
      (pair-cong-triangle₂ (comp-unitˡ f ▷ pr₁) (comp-unitˡ g ▷ pr₂))
      (pair-pre-cong-triangle₂ (id C′ ∘ pr₁) (id D′ ∘ pr₂) h e k))
